about: Chicago's preconfigured landmarks, written as of 1986.

landmarks.name: Sears Tower
landmarks.text: The tallest building in the world, 110 storeys of black aluminium and bronze glass in bundled tubes on Wacker Drive. The Skydeck on the 103rd floor sees four states on a clear day.

landmarks.name: John Hancock Center
landmarks.text: 'Big John', the tapering black tower with its exposed X-braces on the Magnificent Mile. Apartments sit above the offices, and the Signature Room crowns it.

landmarks.name: Wrigley Field
landmarks.text: The Cubs' ivy-walled ballpark in Lakeview, the last in the majors without lights: every home game is played in daylight. Neighbours sell seats on their rooftops across Waveland Avenue.

landmarks.name: Comiskey Park
landmarks.text: The White Sox's 1910 'Baseball Palace of the World' on the South Side, with its exploding scoreboard. Disco Demolition Night ended in a riot here in 1979.

landmarks.name: Chicago Stadium
landmarks.text: 'The Madhouse on Madison', the old barn where the Blackhawks play to the roar of its pipe organ. The Bulls' second-year guard Michael Jordan scored 63 in a playoff game at Boston this spring.

landmarks.name: Soldier Field
landmarks.text: The colonnaded lakefront stadium of the Bears, champions of Super Bowl XX in January. Ditka, Payton and the Fridge have the whole city singing the Super Bowl Shuffle.

landmarks.name: Art Institute of Chicago
landmarks.text: The Beaux-Arts museum on Michigan Avenue guarded by two bronze lions. Seurat's Sunday on La Grande Jatte, Hopper's Nighthawks and American Gothic hang inside.

landmarks.name: Field Museum
landmarks.text: The marble natural history museum on the lakefront, its great hall dominated by two fighting elephants. Egyptian tombs downstairs and the man-eating lions of Tsavo upstairs.

landmarks.name: Shedd Aquarium
landmarks.text: The octagonal Beaux-Arts aquarium on the lake, with a coral reef tank in its rotunda where a diver feeds the sharks. A new oceanarium for whales and dolphins is being planned beside it.

landmarks.name: Adler Planetarium
landmarks.text: The 1930 planetarium on Northerly Island's point, the first in the Western Hemisphere. Its steps have the best view of the skyline across the harbour.

landmarks.name: Museum of Science and Industry
landmarks.find: Museum of Science and Industry, Chicago
landmarks.text: The great columned palace left from the 1893 World's Fair in Jackson Park. Visitors go down a real coal mine and through the captured U-505 submarine.

landmarks.name: Water Tower
landmarks.text: The castellated limestone water tower that survived the Great Fire of 1871, now a tourist office among the Magnificent Mile shops. Water Tower Place's atrium mall is across the street.

landmarks.name: Navy Pier
landmarks.text: The half-mile municipal pier of 1916, mostly empty and slowly decaying, used for the odd festival. The city keeps talking about what to do with it.

landmarks.name: Merchandise Mart
landmarks.text: The Kennedy family's enormous wholesale market on the river, once the largest building in the world by floor area. The 'L' stops at its own station.

landmarks.name: Tribune Tower
landmarks.text: The Gothic home of the Chicago Tribune on Michigan Avenue, its walls set with stones from the Great Wall, the Alamo and Westminster Abbey. WGN broadcasts from its studios.

landmarks.name: Wrigley Building
landmarks.text: The gleaming white terracotta headquarters of the chewing-gum empire at the Michigan Avenue bridge, floodlit every night. Its clock tower faces the Tribune across the street.

landmarks.name: Marina City
landmarks.text: Bertrand Goldberg's twin 'corncob' towers on the river, with their parking spirals and a marina underneath. Cars sometimes go over the edge in the movies.

landmarks.name: Buckingham Fountain
landmarks.text: The great pink-marble fountain of Grant Park, its jets and coloured lights playing every summer evening. The skyline lights up behind it.

landmarks.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
landmarks.text: The free city zoo on the lakeshore north of downtown, with its great apes house and the farm-in-the-zoo. Joggers circle it along the lagoon.

landmarks.name: Chicago Board of Trade
landmarks.text: The Art Deco tower at the end of LaSalle Street's canyon, with a faceless statue of Ceres on top. Traders in the pits below set the world price of grain and pork bellies.

landmarks.name: Union Station
landmarks.text: The Beaux-Arts station by the river with its skylit Great Hall and marble staircases. Amtrak and the commuter lines leave from underneath.

landmarks.name: Chicago Theatre
landmarks.text: The 1921 movie palace on State Street with its giant vertical sign, saved from demolition and reopening this September as a live venue. Frank Sinatra is booked for the opening.

landmarks.name: Daley Center Picasso
landmarks.text: The untitled 50-foot steel Picasso in Daley Plaza, a woman or a baboon depending on who you ask. Kids slide down its base at lunchtime.

landmarks.name: State of Illinois Center
landmarks.text: Helmut Jahn's new glass wedge of state offices with a 17-storey atrium, hot in summer and cold in winter. Chicagoans call it the spaceship.

landmarks.name: Amoco Building
landmarks.text: The marble-clad tower of Standard Oil, the city's second tallest, overlooking Grant Park. Its Carrara marble panels are already bowing in the lake wind.

landmarks.name: Biograph Theater
landmarks.text: The Lincoln Avenue cinema where John Dillinger was shot by the FBI in 1934 after watching Manhattan Melodrama. Still showing first-run films.

landmarks.name: Green Mill
landmarks.text: Al Capone's favourite jazz club in Uptown, his booth still facing both doors. Poetry slams have just started on Sunday nights.

landmarks.name: The Second City
landmarks.find: The Second City, 1616 North Wells Street
landmarks.text: The improv theatre in Old Town where Belushi, Aykroyd and Bill Murray learned the trade. Two shows a night, and an improv set after for free.

landmarks.name: Maxwell Street Market
landmarks.text: The Sunday open-air market on Maxwell and Halsted, all used tools, hot dogs with grilled onions and electric blues on the sidewalk. Anything stolen in Chicago shows up here eventually.

landmarks.name: Hull House
landmarks.text: Jane Addams's settlement house of 1889, its last buildings preserved on the University of Illinois campus. It once fed and taught the whole immigrant West Side.

landmarks.name: Robie House
landmarks.text: Frank Lloyd Wright's long, low Prairie School house of 1910 in Hyde Park. The university uses it for offices.

landmarks.name: Rockefeller Memorial Chapel
landmarks.text: The University of Chicago's Gothic chapel, its tower holding the second-largest carillon in the world. The quadrangles around it look like Oxford.

landmarks.name: O'Hare International Airport
landmarks.text: The busiest airport in the world, on the city's far northwest edge. Delays here ripple across the whole country.

landmarks.name: Cabrini-Green
landmarks.text: The Near North Side public housing towers, a short walk and a world away from the Gold Coast. Gangs control the high-rises; police rarely go in without backup.

landmarks.name: Chinatown Gate
landmarks.text: The gate over Wentworth Avenue into Chinatown, by the On Leong building with its pagoda towers. Restaurants and herbalists line the street.
